tables.name: head_frame_definition
rows: unit vector tragion_R -> tragion_L (+x = subject's left = viewer's right)
plane through tragion_L, tragion_R and the midpoint of orbitale_L/orbitale_R (living-subject Frankfort horizontal)
normal to FH plane, pointing up (toward vertex)
x cross y: forward, out of the face toward a frontal camera (right-handed)
Blender X = x/1000, Blender Y = -z/1000, Blender Z = y/1000 (metres, Z-up, face looking -Y)
FLAME: metres, +X subject's left, +Y up, face toward +Z: same axes as this frame, but origin and FH tilt must be re-solved
matches face3d/synthetic.py conventions (+x subject's left, +y up, +z toward frontal camera, mm)
after sampling or fitting, recompute the frame from the four frame landmarks and re-express all points
tables.notes: Using tragion rather than bony porion makes the frame observable from photos; offset of t-or' line from bony po-or is a few degrees at most (unquantified here).

tables.name: landmark_definitions
rows: highest point of the head in the midline with the head in FH (hair compressed)
midline point of the hairline on the forehead
soft-tissue glabella g': most prominent midline point between the brows
soft-tissue nasion n': deepest midline point of the frontonasal curve (= sellion within ~0-5 mm)
pronasale: most anterior midline point of the nasal tip
subnasale: junction of columella and upper lip in the midline
labrale superius: midpoint of the upper vermilion border
stomion: midline point of the lip junction, lips closed relaxed
labrale inferius: midpoint of the lower vermilion border
sublabiale (soft-tissue B'): deepest midline point of the labiomental fold
soft-tissue pogonion pg': most anterior midline chin point in FH
soft-tissue gnathion gn' (cephalometric): midway pg'-me' on the chin contour
soft-tissue menton me': lowest midline chin point in FH (= Farkas 'gn')
opisthocranion: midline point of the occiput farthest from glabella
tragion: notch at the upper margin of the tragus
soft-tissue orbitale or': skin over the lowest point of the infraorbital rim
pupil centre (= corneal apex for depth), far gaze
endocanthion: inner corner of the palpebral fissure
exocanthion: outer corner of the palpebral fissure
palpebrale superius: highest point of the upper lid margin
palpebrale inferius: lowest point of the lower lid margin
alare: most lateral point of the alar contour
alar curvature (crest) point: most posterolateral point of the alar base groove
soft-tissue zygion zy': most lateral point over the zygomatic arch
soft-tissue gonion go': most lateral-inferior point of the jaw angle
superaurale: highest point of the free margin of the auricle
subaurale: lowest point of the earlobe
euryon: most lateral point of the head (parietal)
tables.notes: FH and prn definitions are sourced; gn' vs me' naming is contested (Farkas 'gn' = lowest chin point = me' here). Bilateral ids carry suffix _L (+x) / _R (-x).

tables.name: mean_landmarks_male_european_young_adult
tables.units: mm, FH head frame (origin mid-tragion; +x subject's left, +y up, +z forward)
tables.population: male, European-ancestry young adult (~18-35 y); synthesised to reproduce Farkas-NAW / ANSUR-type chords
tables.notes: Expert synthesis, NOT a published coordinate set. Only n-me mean and a few SDs are sourced. Profile depths (z) are the least certain values (+/-8 mm on the t->face offset). SDs are the square roots of the diagonal of the factor covariance below; SD 0 on tragion y/z is by frame construction. Replace with FLAME-2023-Open / 3DFN / CAESAR-derived values when computed.

rows: knowledge (Farkas NAW; Kosovo-Albanian sample within 1 mm)
mean knowledge; SD sourced (arXiv 2304.07175 copy of Farkas SDs)
knowledge (soft-tissue jaw-angle width, not caliper on bone)

tables.name: tragion_distances
tables.notes: chord = 3D tragion-to-landmark distance (Farkas-style t-n, t-sn, t-gn 'face depths'); fh_depth = forward distance in the FH frame (what perspective arithmetic needs). Derived from the synthesised configuration; plausible error +/-8 mm on depths. The library's earlier working value of 100 mm for prn-to-tragion depth is low for adult European males under this model (see note).

tables.name: profile_depths_behind_pronasale
tables.units: mm along FH z (pronasale z minus landmark z)
rows: cheek silhouette, frontal view, alar level (not a landmark)
tables.notes: Perspective depth levers. Library notes previously used alar base ~20, eye corners 35-45, cheek contour 60-80, tragion 90-120 (100 nominal); this model gives larger values for alar base, cheek and tragion. East Asian faces: subtract ~3-6 mm from radix/nasal-tip rows (lower projection).

tables.name: factor_sigmas_male
tables.units: mm per unit loading (size: fractional CV)
tables.notes: Factor SDs fitted (NNLS + ridge, floor 0.5x prior guess) so implied chord SDs reproduce recalled Farkas/ANSUR SDs. Covariance = L L^T + diag(residual^2) with L[:,k] = sigma_k * loading_k. Loadings are in table factor_loadings; 'size' loading = mean coordinates (isometric scaling about the mid-tragion origin).

tables.name: factor_sigmas_female
tables.units: mm per unit loading (size: fractional CV)
tables.notes: Factor SDs fitted (NNLS + ridge, floor 0.5x prior guess) so implied chord SDs reproduce recalled Farkas/ANSUR SDs. Covariance = L L^T + diag(residual^2) with L[:,k] = sigma_k * loading_k. Loadings are in table factor_loadings; 'size' loading = mean coordinates (isometric scaling about the mid-tragion origin).

tables.name: factor_loadings
tables.units: mm displacement per mm of factor sigma (unitless direction weights); lower_face_height and face_depth weights scale with position (shown for the male mean; recompute from female mean with the same rules)
tables.population: both sexes (rules identical; numeric weights shown for male mean)
tables.notes: Expert-structured integration factors (size, vertical face, facial depth, mandibular projection, widths, nose, orbit spacing, lips, mouth width, cephalic index, brow, upper-face height, ear length/protrusion, soft tissue, eye opening, vault). Rules: lower_face_height dy = -(y_n - y)/100 for lower-face points (chin dz = -0.15*that; gonion dy at half weight); face_depth dz = clip(z/100, 0, 1.25) for every non-ear/non-vault point.

tables.name: residual_sd
tables.units: mm. total = residual SD per coordinate; asym = part independent per side (rest is shared mirror-symmetrically by L and R)
tables.notes: Includes landmark-definition noise for poorly defined points (v, tr, op, eu, zy, go, me). Tragion residual is zero because the frame is built on it. Residual covariance: diagonal total^2; between L and R of the same landmark, (total^2 - asym^2) with the x term negated (mirror symmetry). Midline x residual = lateral deviation of the midline.

tables.name: implied_chord_correlations_male
tables.notes: Implied by the factor covariance; expected empirical ranges: widths among widths r~0.3-0.6, heights among heights 0.4-0.8 (nested chords higher), width-height 0.1-0.35, en-en weakly coupled (~0.1-0.3). Replace with a FLAME/3DFN-derived covariance when available.

tables.name: perspective_magnification_nose_vs_tragion
tables.units: ratio (d + depth) / d; d = camera to pronasale, m
tables.notes: Pinhole arithmetic. A 10 mm error in the assumed depth changes the 0.5 m ratio by 0.02 (2%), comparable to the CV of zy-zy.

scalp shell girth near g'/op level
face height marginal (sellion is the deepest nasal-root point)
vertical, tragion to vertex, head in FH
fit sex x ancestry x age cells
tables.population: US Army 2010-2012 survey; public release 4,082 M + 1,986 F [ANSUR II page]
tables.notes: Sample split sourced (public 4,082/1,986; full survey 7,435/3,922 per the technical report, contested). Column names and mean ranges are recalled and must be checked against the CSV; compute means, SDs and the 13x13 correlation matrix per Gender x DODRace directly from the file. ANSUR has no t-n, t-sn or prn depth: it constrains sizes, not profile depths.

tables.name: age_drift_per_decade_after_30
tables.units: mm per decade in FH frame (approximately linear 30-70 y; accelerates after ~50)
rows: ear length grows ~1.5-2.5 mm/decade, mostly lobule
upper lip lengthens, vermilion thins and inverts
jowling blurs and widens the jaw angle
dermatochalasis / aponeurotic ptosis lower the visible lid margin
tables.population: adults of European ancestry (direction general; magnitudes rough)
tables.notes: Cranium, canthal width and nasion are stable in adulthood. Hairline (tr) recession in men is too variable to put in a mean. Widen the prior SD by ~10-20% per decade after 50.
